summary: Sisir Roy works in philosophy and other fields. He studied under Debabrata Sensharma, was a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute, and was affiliated with the National Institute of Advanced Studies in 2009.
Sita Krishna Nambiar, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Paul Hacker. She held a post at Indraprastha College for Women.

Sita Ram Roy, active in history, archaeology, and Indology, earned his doctorate under Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma. He held positions at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, Gaya Museum, and the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Bihar.
Siu-tong Kwan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti and also studied under Zhihua Yao.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indology scholar who served as a Sanskrit teacher at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, where his posts are attested in 1892 and 1929.

Sivananda Saraswati (1887–1963) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Thanjavur Medical College and founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.
Siyong Liang (1904–1954) was an archaeologist and historian. He pursued his education at Tsinghua University from circa 1916 to 1923 and at Harvard University from circa 1924 to 1930.
Smita Halder works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar and was a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

So Takahashi (born 1938) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. He held posts as associate professor and professor at Meijo University between 1977 and 1991.

Sodo Mori (born 1934) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, he was a professor at Josai University and Aichi Gakuin University.
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure. He studied at Antai-ji from 1949 to 1957 under Kodo Sawaki, and also studied under Ekō Hashimoto.
Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, as well as under traditional teacher Gempo Yamamoto.

Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University under numerous teachers, including Dokutan Sōsan. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from 1911 to 1923.
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Nihon University and held a post at Kanagawa University.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy after studying at Nihon University and under Seisetsu Seki, Jirōkichi Yamada, and Bokuo Seki. He served as professor and president of Hanazono University and abbot of Koho-in.

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Delhi, the University of Cambridge, and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, founding Rigpa in 1975.

Soiku Shigematsu (born 1943) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Kyoto University. Active in Buddhist studies, he was an English literature professor at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and professor at Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).
Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) worked in Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University in 1974 and as a teacher at Zuigan-ji between 1992 and 1996.
Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Kōsen Imakita and Soyen Shaku. He founded Ryobokai in 1901, the Ryobokai Dojo of North America in 1906, and Ningen Zen.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tokyo University of the Arts and under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku. He founded the First Zen Institute of America in 1930.
